title: Bend It
blurb: Draw the shot you want with one finger. Let go, and the kicker reads your line and hits it.
description: Bend It is a penalty game with exactly one control: you draw a line on the screen, and when you let go the kicker interprets it and strikes. Draw straight for a driven shot, bow the line to bend it round the keeper, arc it up and over for a chip — the shape you draw is the shot, and where your line finishes is where the ball finishes. Reading a drawing is a fit rather than a parse: your line is least-squares fitted onto the space of shots a kicker can actually strike, so a shaky hand still produces a clean shot and the same swipe always produces the same kick. The finish is always clamped inside the goal, and once the ball leaves the boot nothing steers it. The goalkeeper is not a coin flip: it reads only the first fraction of the flight, dives for where it thinks the ball is going, gets one mid-flight correction of its line but never of its height, and remembers where your last few penalties finished — so a shape that works stops working. Everything is procedural: mown turf, penalty-area markings, a goal with a rippling net, and a procedural humanoid kicker and keeper. Portrait phone first; mouse on desktop through the same one gesture.
